assessments.source_element: knowledge of measuring ingredients, mixing batter, and baking time
assessments.target_element: learned model parameters, features, and training procedures
assessments.rationale: Both refer to reusable procedural knowledge that can be transferred from a source to a target; the analogy correctly captures the idea of reusing learned components.
The original cake corresponds directly to the source task whose learned representation is transferred.
The new cake represents the target task that receives the transferred knowledge.

assessments.source_element: swapping cocoa powder for vanilla extract (minor adjustment)
assessments.target_element: fine‑tuning or adapting the model to the new task
assessments.rationale: Minor ingredient changes map well onto fine‑tuning, where only a small part of the model is adjusted for the new domain.

structural_issues: Baking is a deterministic physical process, while model training is statistical; the analogy glosses over this fundamental difference.
The analogy assumes the source and target tasks are sufficiently similar; it does not capture cases where domains are highly dissimilar and transfer fails.
result.rationale: All four core mappings align logically and consistently with the concepts of transfer learning. Minor structural mismatches (deterministic vs probabilistic nature, similarity requirement) are noted but do not undermine the overall soundness of the analogy.
